_comment: Agent-maintained crypto-regulation jurisdictions. Merged over the curated seed in jurisdictions.ts (an entry here overrides the seed by id, or adds a new one). Shape: { id, name, iso (ISO-3166 numeric string[]), lat, lon, status (implemented|in-progress|none), headline, summary, soWhat?, keyDates?, sources[{name,url}] }. Invalid entries are dropped at load. The agent updates this each run — see agent/INGEST.md.

jurisdictions.name: European Union
jurisdictions.headline: MiCA transitional period ended 1 July 2026 — only ~244 of 1,200+ VASPs converted
jurisdictions.summary: MiCA's national grandfathering period expired on 1 July 2026 as scheduled. ESMA ordered any CASP without full MiCA authorisation to wind down EU activity in an orderly manner. As the deadline arrived only around 244 of the roughly 1,200+ previously-registered VASPs (17-20%) had secured full CASP authorisation, led by Germany (57 licences) and France (26); NCAs are coordinating with EBA and AMLA on enforcement against firms that kept operating unauthorised.
jurisdictions.soWhat: The grandfathering cliff has now actually happened, not just been scheduled — treat any EU-facing counterparty absent from the ESMA CASP register as operating illegally, a hard trigger to suspend the relationship rather than a future watch item.

sources.name: ESMA — Statement on the end of transitional periods under MiCA
CoinDesk — Europe's unlicensed crypto firms face 'wipeout' as MiCA transition deadline falls

jurisdictions.name: Bahrain
jurisdictions.headline: CBB crypto-asset licensing regime
jurisdictions.summary: The Central Bank of Bahrain runs a clear crypto-asset module (CRA) that licenses permitted activities; unlicensed crypto activity is prohibited.
jurisdictions.soWhat: A Gulf early-mover with explicit licensing — check a Bahraini counterparty's CBB authorisation.

jurisdictions.name: Thailand
jurisdictions.headline: SEC licensing; payments prohibited
jurisdictions.summary: Thailand's SEC licenses digital-asset businesses and operators; trading and holding are legal, but using crypto for payments is banned.

jurisdictions.name: Indonesia
jurisdictions.headline: Supervision moved to OJK; payments banned
jurisdictions.summary: Crypto trading is regulated (oversight transferred from Bappebti to the financial regulator OJK); it is legal to trade and hold but not to pay with.

jurisdictions.name: Philippines
jurisdictions.headline: BSP VASP licensing + SEC rules
jurisdictions.summary: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas licenses Virtual Asset Service Providers, with the SEC adding rules for crypto offerings and exchanges.

jurisdictions.name: Argentina
jurisdictions.headline: CNV VASP registration enforced
jurisdictions.summary: The securities regulator CNV enforced a VASP registration regime (Resolution 1058/2025) for crypto firms serving Argentine users.

jurisdictions.name: Kenya
jurisdictions.headline: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act 2025
jurisdictions.summary: Kenya's VASP Act (2025) is in force, with the Central Bank and Capital Markets Authority setting rules for licensing and bank integration.
jurisdictions.soWhat: East Africa's new licensing regime — a reference point for the region's high-adoption markets.

jurisdictions.name: Gibraltar
jurisdictions.headline: DLT Provider framework (since 2018)
jurisdictions.summary: Gibraltar's GFSC has licensed Distributed Ledger Technology providers under a principles-based framework since 2018 — one of the earliest dedicated regimes.

jurisdictions.name: Cayman Islands
jurisdictions.headline: Virtual Asset (Service Providers) Act
jurisdictions.summary: Crypto businesses must register or be licensed under the Cayman VASP Act before operating — a major offshore fund/crypto domicile.
jurisdictions.soWhat: A common domicile for crypto funds and issuers — VASP registration status is a key diligence point.

jurisdictions.name: Liechtenstein
jurisdictions.headline: Token & TT Service Provider Act (Blockchain Act)
jurisdictions.summary: Liechtenstein's TVTG (Blockchain Act, in force since 2020) provides a comprehensive token-economy framework with registered service providers.

jurisdictions.name: Türkiye
jurisdictions.headline: CMB licensing rolling out; payments banned
jurisdictions.summary: Türkiye passed a crypto law bringing exchanges under Capital Markets Board licensing; trading and holding are permitted but paying with crypto is banned.

jurisdictions.name: Saudi Arabia
jurisdictions.headline: Asset, not legal tender; framework forming
jurisdictions.summary: Crypto is treated as an asset (not legal tender); banks need explicit SAMA approval, and regulators are running pilots before finalising a national framework.

jurisdictions.name: Qatar
jurisdictions.headline: QFC Digital Assets framework; payments banned
jurisdictions.summary: The Qatar Financial Centre operates a Digital Assets framework/regulatory zone, while crypto payments remain prohibited outside it.

jurisdictions.name: Israel
jurisdictions.headline: Securities-led; AML in force
jurisdictions.summary: Crypto is not legal tender; the ISA treats many tokens as securities and AML/CFT obligations apply, with a dedicated framework still developing.

jurisdictions.name: Vietnam
jurisdictions.headline: Digital assets recognised; 5-year pilot
jurisdictions.summary: The Law on Digital Technology Industry (effective 1 Jan 2026) recognises digital assets as legal property and launches a five-year trading pilot.

jurisdictions.name: Pakistan
jurisdictions.headline: Ban lifted; PVARA stood up (2026)
jurisdictions.summary: In April 2026 Pakistan replaced its prior ban with a framework, creating a Crypto Council and the Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority (PVARA).

jurisdictions.name: Kazakhstan
jurisdictions.headline: AIFC zone licensing; national rules forming
jurisdictions.summary: Crypto exchanges can be licensed within the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC); a broader national framework and CBDC work are developing.

jurisdictions.name: Mexico
jurisdictions.headline: Fintech Law; no dedicated crypto regime
jurisdictions.summary: Mexico's Fintech Law touches virtual assets and the central bank restricts bank involvement, but there is no comprehensive dedicated crypto framework.

jurisdictions.name: Colombia
jurisdictions.headline: Banks barred; sandbox + draft rules
jurisdictions.summary: Financial institutions are restricted from facilitating crypto, but regulators have run sandboxes and are working toward a clearer framework.

jurisdictions.name: New Zealand
jurisdictions.headline: Legal; supervised under existing law
jurisdictions.summary: Crypto is legal and supervised through existing financial-services and AML rules (FMA / DIA), without a bespoke dedicated regime.

jurisdictions.name: Egypt
jurisdictions.headline: Trading banned (CBE Law 194)
jurisdictions.summary: Egypt prohibits crypto trading under Central Bank Law No. 194, even as it pursues a national blockchain strategy.
jurisdictions.soWhat: No legitimate onshore crypto activity — treat any Egypt-nexus crypto flow with heightened scrutiny.

jurisdictions.name: Bangladesh
jurisdictions.headline: Comprehensive ban
jurisdictions.summary: Bangladesh maintains a complete prohibition on cryptocurrency use and trading.

jurisdictions.name: Morocco
jurisdictions.headline: Ban in place; framework drafted
jurisdictions.summary: Crypto trading is banned, though Morocco's central bank has drafted a framework that could legalise and regulate it.

jurisdictions.name: Russia
jurisdictions.headline: Mining legal, domestic payments banned; cross-border trade law now in force
jurisdictions.summary: Russia legalised and regulates crypto mining but bans domestic crypto payments. On 1 July 2026 its experimental cross-border trade regime — allowing Bitcoin and stablecoins to settle foreign trade (oil, metals, grain) through eight licensed venues, with reporting to the Central Bank and Rosfinmonitoring above a low ruble threshold — converted from pilot to statute.
jurisdictions.soWhat: Sanctions-evasion nexus — a formal, licensed settlement rail now exists outside SWIFT; treat Russian cross-border crypto settlement, and the eight newly licensed venues specifically, as elevated risk.

keyDates.label: Cross-border trade crypto-payments law in force

sources.name: Yahoo Finance — Russia locks in July 1 crypto payments regime to bypass sanctions
